_about: What the nightly run tests. ONE primary variable per batch of 3 videos; every other test stays fixed at its `control` option. The Monday plan (PLAN.md) assigns the options per video, the weekly review (REVIEW.md) measures the batch and closes it. Times are Europe/Madrid; the audience is mostly US (NY = Madrid - 6 h, LA = Madrid - 9 h).

protocol.primary_metric: watch_pct = average watch time / video length, per network, averaged over the networks the video went to. Views depend too much on algorithm luck; they are reported, not decisive.

windows.note: Verdicts use the 7-day figures. The 48 h figures are only an early read for the notification.

protocol.baseline: median watch_pct of the last 5 videos with role `base` or `control`. The 7 reels published before 2026-11-04 count as base.

roles.control: uses the control option, to refresh the baseline
roles.base: tests nothing (special-date or themed reels, or a day with no test); counts for the baseline

protocol.success: the variant beats the baseline by more than 20% on watch_pct in at least 2 of the 3 videos of the batch
protocol.failure: the variant is worse than the baseline by more than 20% in at least 2 of the 3 videos
protocol.inconclusive: anything else. Not 'it does not work': repeat the batch once with 3 new videos; if still inconclusive, close it as 'no detectable difference' and keep the control.

outcomes.adopt: status decided, the variant becomes the new `control` for every video
outcomes.repeat: same test, a new batch id

protocol.side_experiment: `variants.tiktok_mode` (manual vs api) keeps running on its own rule (about 1 reel in 4) and is analysed on TikTok only, by REVIEW.md. It is not a variable of the batch.

batch.hypothesis: A hook that opens with a surprising statement and then asks the question holds more viewers than a direct question, because it gives a reason to stay in the first 3 seconds.
batch.note: The third video (2026-11-11) is added by the Monday plan of 2026-11-09.

queue.why: does the 8 am NY slot beat 2:30 pm NY
does a second signature touch help

time_slots.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

options.question: the hook is a direct question ('Why do cats purr?')
options.statement: a surprising statement, then the question ('Slaves didn't build the pyramids. So who did?')

hook_style.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

options.teaser: hook + one line that teases the twist, without giving the answer
options.question_cta: hook + a question inviting comments ('Did you know this? 👇')

caption_style.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

personality.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

format.rule: Not an experiment: the formats vary on purpose so the channel does not look like a mass-produced series. Use the format with the fewest reels in the log (ties: the one used longest ago). Never the same format twice in a row. Themed (special-date) reels may use any format. The review records the format of every video and mentions it if it clearly explains a result.
